A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same position paper and CLIP unlearning case study. All 21 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support matching text, equations, figures, and tables.

before.justification: V1 reports original CLIP unlearning experiments on ImgnetDogs and CompCars-S, including zero-shot generalization, OxfordPet robustness, and sample-count analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds coarse-grained concept-removal experiments on ImgnetDogs in Table 4.

M1.justification: NHL+KL is renamed HGA+KL, retaining the hinge loss, proxy forgetting images, and coarse- and fine-grained KL regularizers. The additional equations explain existing components; no new algorithmic component or procedural revision is documented.

E1.justification: V2 adds an evaluated scenario that removes coarse categories, such as Retriever and Setter, together with their subordinate fine classes. V1 discussed higher-level forgetting as a possible extension. This broadens task requirements within ImgnetDogs while retaining the existing datasets and domains.

E2.justification: The comparator sets remain unchanged in corresponding experiments. V2's new coarse-grained comparison uses the same GA, GDiff, GA+KL, Relabeling, SalUn, ME+GD, Task Vector, and NPO+KL baselines already compared in v1.

E3.justification: V2 Table 4 introduces evaluation that minimizes both coarse and fine recognition on the forgetting set; the existing fine-grained protocol preserves coarse recognition. Retained experiments keep their settings. The new coarse-specific aggregation of quality and utility is not explicitly defined.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.2 adds an empirical analysis of target granularity using coarse-category removal results. Existing difficulty-level and OxfordPet robustness analyses remain unchanged. The sample-count analysis was already in v1 Appendix F.1 and is merely moved into the main text.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests for its experiments. V2 continues the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 Table 4 adds coarse-grained results, including Q-U scores of 90.81 for HGA+KL and 87.82 for NPO+KL. These are new-task results, not improvements over the earlier fine-grained setting. All matched existing result tables retain their numerical values.

T1.justification: V2 displays equations for the KL regularizers and combined objective already described in v1 Section 4.1.2 and Table 9. No new theoretical result, formal assumption, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced; the challenges section is conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion newly foreground discussion of knowledge-tracing FMU's nontrivial challenges as a contribution. The central advocacy of knowledge-level unlearning requests and the illustrative role of the CLIP case study remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V1 briefly questioned knowledge boundaries and evaluation standards. V2 Section 4 develops a substantial account of heterogeneous knowledge representations, ambiguous removal boundaries, and genuine erasure versus output suppression. Section 5.2 also adds interpretation of how granularity and model memorization jointly affect unlearning difficulty.

D1.justification: Dataset construction, prompts, hyperparameters, optimizer, training duration, hardware, checkpoint selection, and code access remain unchanged. The additional loss expressions restate regularizers and the weighted objective already documented in v1; moving the project link into the abstract does not change access.

R1.justification: All 102 cited works match across versions, and the related-work positioning remains substantively unchanged. Changes such as correcting the GPT-4 report's authors and switching to author-year citations are bibliographic or presentation edits.

P1.justification: V2 inserts a challenges section, updates the abstract and roadmap, moves the sample-count discussion into the main results, and groups Appendices A-F as A.1-A.6. Naming and grammar are standardized, while most existing prose and the narrative order remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 substantially reformats the document into TMLR style, changing typography, margins, running headers, author layout, and table widths. Figure 1 is redrawn and recaptioned, the coarse-grained results table is added, and v1 Table 14 moves into the main text as v2 Table 5.

improvement.justification: The coarse-grained experiment modestly strengthens the empirical illustration, while Section 4 makes the conceptual and verification challenges clearer. These gains are limited by the new experiment's underspecified training adaptation and quality/utility aggregation. The existing method, results, and documented robustness limitations otherwise remain unchanged.
